issue_context.title: Homekit throws an error about z2m thermostat after 2021.11.1 update
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hello again, @bdraco!

After updating the HA to the 2021.11.1, an error began to appear in the logs about the [Siterwell TRV from Z2M](https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/devices/GS361A-H04.html). But the modes are correctly changed both through HK and through HA.

I'm not sure which side this is on (HA or Z2M), but first I decided to write here.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.11.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2021.10.6

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

homekit, mqtt

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homekit/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Logger: homeassistant.helpers.event
Source: components/homekit/type_thermostats.py:466
First occurred: 7 ноября 2021 г., 18:37:43 (20 occurrences)
Last logged: 06:43:18

Error while processing state change for climate.siterwell_trv
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/event.py", line 269, in _async_state_change_dispatcher
    hass.async_run_hass_job(job, event)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/core.py", line 433, in async_run_hass_job
    hassjob.target(*args)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/homekit/accessories.py", line 389, in async_update_event_state_callback
    self.async_update_state_callback(event.data.get("new_state"))
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/homekit/accessories.py", line 411, in async_update_state_callback
    self.async_update_state(new_state)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/homekit/type_thermostats.py", line 444, in async_update_state
    self._async_update_state(new_state)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/homekit/type_thermostats.py", line 466, in _async_update_state
    homekit_hvac_action = HC_HASS_TO_HOMEKIT_ACTION[hvac_action]
KeyError: 'None'
```


### Additional information

_No response_

Hey there @bdraco, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`homekit`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L227) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

It also throws that error with version 2021.10.6 for me, just a line more :P
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/event.py", line 269, in _async_state_change_dispatcher
    hass.async_run_hass_job(job, event)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/core.py", line 433, in async_run_hass_job
    hassjob.target(*args)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/homekit/accessories.py", line 389, in async_update_event_state_callback
    self.async_update_state_callback(event.data.get("new_state"))
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/homekit/accessories.py", line 411, in async_update_state_callback

  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/homekit/type_thermostats.py", line 467, in _async_update_state
    homekit_hvac_action = HC_HASS_TO_HOMEKIT_ACTION[hvac_action]
KeyError: 'None'
```

But it does at least still show up using homekit.

I currently do not know whether hvac_action should always be present (at least it appears to be expected) or not given e.g. target_temp is checked for None in Line 502
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/homekit/type_thermostats.py#L465

However, zigbee2mqtt does not fetch all values properly either.

```    
    "position": null,
    "running_state": null
```

For reference: https://github.com/Koenkk/zigbee2mqtt/issues/8813

review_comments: If it's really getting quoted "None", this is a bug in the source data and probably shouldn't be changed in HomeKit.
In any case, if a non-standard value appears, it will lead to an error and crash thermostat. I think it might be helpful to add an extra check.

HVAC mode checked in as same way.
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f8a66ec1f2767c53553aeddb20ec9bc1c48cd1ed/homeassistant/components/homekit/type_thermostats.py#L453

The integration is responsible for validating data before setting it in state machine.  I'd consider it a bug in the integration that is injecting bad state data in the state machine since anything reading it is going to have a problem.   We shouldn't add workarounds to every integration that is consuming the data, we should fix it at the source.

If the value is passed in as `None` (no quotes), the climate entity won't set the property.
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/climate/__init__.py#L298

I agree its a bug `handle_action_received` is lacking validation, and doesn't handle the `null`/`None` case.  It looks like its being converted to a string.
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/mqtt/climate.py#L407

`handle_swing_mode_received` does validation so it could be used as a template to fix it. to ensure that `hvac_action` is only a valid action as defined by the developer docs or `None` https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/climate/#hvac-action

Example
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/mqtt/climate.py#L509
So, I understood you. How do we fix this bug? :)

Modify `handle_action_received` in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/mqtt/climate.py#L407 to use the same type of validation that https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/mqtt/climate.py#L509 uses

Ohh... @bdraco Thanks a lot for the tip and review! 
P.S. If you still have time, please take a look at my HK [related issue](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/59329).
